questions.prompt: Which statement best describes limited liability in a registered company?
options: Shareholders can lose only the unpaid amount on their shares
Directors never have any legal duties
The company cannot own property separately from owners
All shareholders must manage daily operations
questions.correctAnswer: Shareholders can lose only the unpaid amount on their shares
questions.explanation: Limited liability separates the owners' personal wealth from the company's debts, except for the amount they have agreed to invest.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain features of common forms of business ownership.

questions.prompt: A partnership deed is most useful because it
options: sets out partners' rights, duties, profit sharing, and dispute procedures
replaces all accounting records in the business
allows partners to avoid every business risk
turns a partnership into a public company automatically
questions.correctAnswer: sets out partners' rights, duties, profit sharing, and dispute procedures
questions.explanation: A partnership deed reduces misunderstanding by recording how partners will contribute, share profits, make decisions, and handle disputes.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe documents and agreements used to manage partnerships.

questions.prompt: Which factor is an internal strength in a SWOT analysis for a school-based bakery project?
options: A trained member who can prepare quality products
A new competitor opening near the school
A rise in flour prices in the market
A change in county health inspection rules
questions.correctAnswer: A trained member who can prepare quality products
questions.explanation: Strengths are helpful internal conditions controlled by the enterprise, such as skills, equipment, or good systems.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify internal and external factors affecting enterprise performance.

questions.prompt: A cooperative society is different from a sole proprietorship mainly because it
options: is owned and controlled by members for their mutual benefit
must be owned by only one person
cannot distribute services to members
has no need for records or elected officials
questions.correctAnswer: is owned and controlled by members for their mutual benefit
questions.explanation: Cooperatives are member-owned organizations formed to serve common economic or social interests.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare cooperative societies with other forms of business ownership.

questions.prompt: Which action best shows corporate social responsibility by a medium-sized business?
options: Treating waste safely and supporting a community skills project
Selling expired goods quietly to reduce losses
Using false advertisements to increase demand
Refusing to address unsafe working conditions
questions.correctAnswer: Treating waste safely and supporting a community skills project
questions.explanation: Social responsibility requires a business to consider customers, workers, community welfare, and the environment while pursuing its goals.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply ethical and socially responsible practices to business situations.

questions.prompt: A trader separates business cash from personal spending. Which accounting concept is being applied?
options: Business entity concept
Realization concept
Prudence concept
Matching concept
questions.correctAnswer: Business entity concept
questions.explanation: The business entity concept treats the business as separate from the owner for accounting purposes.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify accounting concepts used in business records.

questions.prompt: Which document is normally used to request payment from a buyer after goods are sold on credit?
options: Invoice
Receipt
Pay-in slip
Bank statement
questions.correctAnswer: Invoice
questions.explanation: An invoice states goods or services supplied on credit and the amount the buyer owes.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify source documents used in credit transactions.

questions.prompt: A credit note sent to a customer usually records
options: a reduction in the amount the customer owes
a cash deposit made into the bank
a new loan taken from a bank
the daily cash balance in a till
questions.correctAnswer: a reduction in the amount the customer owes
questions.explanation: A credit note is issued when goods are returned or an overcharge is corrected, reducing the customer's debt.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the purpose of debit and credit notes in business transactions.

questions.prompt: In double-entry bookkeeping, what happens when a business buys equipment for cash?
options: Equipment is debited and cash is credited
Cash is debited and equipment is credited
Purchases are debited and capital is credited
Expenses are credited and sales are debited
questions.correctAnswer: Equipment is debited and cash is credited
questions.explanation: Buying equipment increases an asset account and decreases cash, so equipment is debited and cash is credited.
questions.learningOutcome: Record simple asset transactions using double-entry rules.

questions.prompt: A business pays rent of 12,000 shillings by bank transfer. Which double-entry record is appropriate?
options: Debit rent expense and credit bank
Debit bank and credit rent expense
Debit capital and credit rent expense
Debit sales and credit bank
questions.correctAnswer: Debit rent expense and credit bank
questions.explanation: Rent is an expense, so it is debited; the bank account decreases, so it is credited.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply double-entry rules to expense payments.

questions.prompt: Which transaction increases both assets and capital of a business?
options: Owner introduces cash into the business
Business pays a supplier in cash
Business buys stock on credit
Owner withdraws cash for personal use
questions.correctAnswer: Owner introduces cash into the business
questions.explanation: Capital introduced by the owner increases business cash and increases the owner's claim in the business.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze how transactions affect assets, liabilities, and capital.

questions.prompt: Which transaction decreases both assets and liabilities?
options: Paying a creditor by cheque
Buying goods on credit
Owner bringing cash into the business
Receiving cash from a customer for cash sales
questions.correctAnswer: Paying a creditor by cheque
questions.explanation: Paying a creditor reduces the bank asset and reduces the amount owed to the creditor.
questions.learningOutcome: Determine the effect of business transactions on financial position.

questions.prompt: A trial balance is prepared mainly to check whether
options: total debit balances equal total credit balances
all goods were sold at a profit
cash is kept separately from inventory
every customer has paid in advance
questions.correctAnswer: total debit balances equal total credit balances
questions.explanation: A trial balance tests the arithmetic equality of ledger debit and credit balances, though it does not prove every entry is error-free.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the purpose and limitations of a trial balance.

questions.prompt: Which error would not be revealed by a trial balance?
options: Recording a cash sale in the wrong customer's account with equal debit and credit amounts
Posting a debit entry without a matching credit entry
Adding the credit column incorrectly
Recording one side of a transaction twice
questions.correctAnswer: Recording a cash sale in the wrong customer's account with equal debit and credit amounts
questions.explanation: Errors of commission can leave total debits equal to total credits even though the transaction is posted to the wrong account.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze errors that may or may not affect trial balance agreement.

questions.prompt: A trader has sales of 180,000 shillings, purchases of 105,000 shillings, opening stock of 20,000 shillings, and closing stock of 25,000 shillings. What is the gross profit?
options: 80,000 shillings
75,000 shillings
50,000 shillings
100,000 shillings
questions.correctAnswer: 80,000 shillings
questions.explanation: Cost of goods sold is 20,000 plus 105,000 minus 25,000, which equals 100,000; gross profit is 180,000 minus 100,000.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate gross profit using stock and purchase information.

questions.prompt: If gross profit is 60,000 shillings and operating expenses are 38,500 shillings, what is the net profit?
options: 21,500 shillings
98,500 shillings
60,000 shillings
38,500 shillings
questions.correctAnswer: 21,500 shillings
questions.explanation: Net profit equals gross profit minus operating expenses, so 60,000 minus 38,500 equals 21,500 shillings.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate net profit from gross profit and expense data.

questions.prompt: Which item belongs in a statement of financial position as a current asset?
options: Trade receivables expected within the year
Bank loan repayable after five years
Owner's capital balance
Accrued rent payable
questions.correctAnswer: Trade receivables expected within the year
questions.explanation: Current assets are resources expected to be converted into cash, sold, or used within the operating cycle or one year.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify assets and liabilities for financial statements.

questions.prompt: A business has assets of 240,000 shillings and liabilities of 95,000 shillings. What is the owner's capital?
options: 145,000 shillings
335,000 shillings
95,000 shillings
240,000 shillings
questions.correctAnswer: 145,000 shillings
questions.explanation: Capital equals assets minus liabilities, so 240,000 minus 95,000 equals 145,000 shillings.
questions.learningOutcome: Use the accounting equation to calculate capital.

questions.prompt: A business bought a delivery bicycle for 30,000 shillings. It is expected to have a residual value of 6,000 shillings after four years. Using straight-line depreciation, what is the annual depreciation?
options: 6,000 shillings
7,500 shillings
9,000 shillings
24,000 shillings
questions.correctAnswer: 6,000 shillings
questions.explanation: Straight-line depreciation is cost minus residual value divided by useful life: 30,000 minus 6,000, then divided by four.
questions.learningOutcome: Compute annual depreciation using the straight-line method.

questions.prompt: Why is depreciation charged in financial records?
options: To spread the cost of a non-current asset over the periods it helps generate revenue
To show that cash has been stolen from the business
To remove the need to record asset purchases
To increase the bank balance automatically
questions.correctAnswer: To spread the cost of a non-current asset over the periods it helps generate revenue
questions.explanation: Depreciation matches the asset's cost with the accounting periods that benefit from using it.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the purpose of depreciation in accounting.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes a bank reconciliation statement?
options: A comparison of the cash book bank balance with the bank statement balance
A list of all products held in the store
A record of employees' daily attendance
A document that cancels every bank charge
questions.correctAnswer: A comparison of the cash book bank balance with the bank statement balance
questions.explanation: Bank reconciliation explains timing differences and errors between the business cash book and the bank statement.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the purpose of bank reconciliation.

questions.prompt: A cheque issued to a supplier has not yet been presented to the bank. How should it be treated in bank reconciliation from the bank statement balance?
options: Deduct it as an unpresented cheque
Add it as direct income
Record it as closing inventory
Ignore it because it is not a transaction
questions.correctAnswer: Deduct it as an unpresented cheque
questions.explanation: An unpresented cheque has reduced the cash book but not the bank statement, so it is deducted when reconciling from the bank statement balance.
questions.learningOutcome: Prepare adjustments for timing differences in bank reconciliation.

questions.prompt: Which budget would help a school enterprise estimate expected cash receipts and payments for the next month?
options: Cash budget
Sales invoice
Petty cash voucher
Inventory bin card
questions.correctAnswer: Cash budget
questions.explanation: A cash budget forecasts cash inflows and outflows so the business can plan for surplus or shortage.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify budgets used to plan business cash flows.

questions.prompt: A business expects cash receipts of 86,000 shillings and cash payments of 74,500 shillings in August. What is the expected cash surplus?
options: 11,500 shillings
160,500 shillings
74,500 shillings
9,500 shillings
questions.correctAnswer: 11,500 shillings
questions.explanation: Cash surplus equals receipts minus payments, so 86,000 minus 74,500 equals 11,500 shillings.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate cash surplus or deficit from budget information.

questions.prompt: If actual advertising expense is lower than the budgeted amount, the variance is usually described as
options: favourable because less was spent than planned
adverse because less was spent than planned
irrelevant because expenses cannot be budgeted
a liability because all variances are debts
questions.correctAnswer: favourable because less was spent than planned
questions.explanation: For expenses, spending less than budgeted is normally favourable, provided it does not harm performance.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret favourable and adverse budget variances.

questions.prompt: A small business should investigate an adverse sales variance because it may show that
options: actual sales were lower than planned and action may be needed
customers paid more than expected for every item
the business has no need for stock control
all expenses were paid in advance
questions.correctAnswer: actual sales were lower than planned and action may be needed
questions.explanation: An adverse sales variance can point to weak demand, poor promotion, stock shortages, or pricing problems.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze reasons for variances and recommend business responses.

questions.prompt: Which ratio measures the ability of a business to pay short-term debts using current assets?
options: Current ratio
Gross profit margin
Stock turnover
Return on capital employed
questions.correctAnswer: Current ratio
questions.explanation: The current ratio compares current assets with current liabilities to assess short-term liquidity.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify financial ratios used in business decision making.

questions.prompt: A business has current assets of 120,000 shillings and current liabilities of 60,000 shillings. What is the current ratio?
questions.explanation: Current ratio equals current assets divided by current liabilities, so 120,000 divided by 60,000 is 2:1.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate liquidity ratios from financial information.

questions.prompt: A gross profit margin rises from 20 percent to 35 percent while sales volume is stable. Which interpretation is most reasonable?
options: The business may be controlling cost of goods sold or improving selling prices
The business must have stopped selling goods completely
All credit customers must have paid late
The bank statement must be overdrawn
questions.correctAnswer: The business may be controlling cost of goods sold or improving selling prices
questions.explanation: A higher gross profit margin suggests better control of buying cost, selling price, or product mix before operating expenses.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret changes in profitability ratios for business decisions.

questions.prompt: Which decision best uses accounting information responsibly?
options: Comparing profit, cash flow, and stock records before expanding production
Borrowing heavily because sales increased for one day
Ignoring expenses because customers like the product
Setting prices without checking costs
questions.correctAnswer: Comparing profit, cash flow, and stock records before expanding production
questions.explanation: Good decisions use several financial records together to reduce risk and choose realistic actions.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate financial evidence before making enterprise decisions.

questions.prompt: Which function of money is shown when prices in a supermarket are quoted in shillings?
options: Unit of account
Store of value
Deferred payment
Direct barter
questions.correctAnswer: Unit of account
questions.explanation: Money acts as a unit of account when it provides a common measure for valuing goods and services.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify functions of money in everyday business transactions.

questions.prompt: A farmer saves proceeds from a harvest in a bank account for school fees next term. Which function of money is mainly shown?
options: Store of value
Measure of length
Physical inventory count
Means of production
questions.correctAnswer: Store of value
questions.explanation: Money stores value when it allows purchasing power to be kept for future use.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe how money supports saving and future payments.

questions.prompt: Which service is normally provided by a commercial bank to business customers?
options: Offering current accounts and payment services
Printing official national currency
Setting all school fees in the country
Issuing product quality marks
questions.correctAnswer: Offering current accounts and payment services
questions.explanation: Commercial banks provide accounts, payment services, credit, and other financial services to individuals and businesses.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain services offered by commercial banks to businesses.

questions.prompt: Which institution is responsible for regulating commercial banks and supporting monetary stability in Kenya?
options: Central Bank of Kenya
Kenya Bureau of Standards
Capital Markets Authority
Insurance Regulatory Authority
questions.correctAnswer: Central Bank of Kenya
questions.explanation: The Central Bank of Kenya regulates banks and helps maintain stability in the monetary and financial system.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify financial institutions and their roles in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Which source of finance is most suitable for buying expensive equipment that will serve a business for several years?
options: A medium-term or long-term loan matched to the asset life
Using the daily petty cash float
Delaying all wages indefinitely
Borrowing from customers without records
questions.correctAnswer: A medium-term or long-term loan matched to the asset life
questions.explanation: Long-lived assets are better financed by sources whose repayment period fits the period over which the asset helps the business.
questions.learningOutcome: Select appropriate sources of finance for business needs.

questions.prompt: Why might a business prefer trade credit from suppliers for short-term stock purchases?
options: It allows the business to obtain goods now and pay later within agreed terms
It permanently removes the need to pay for stock
It converts stock into owner's drawings
It always has no cost or conditions
questions.correctAnswer: It allows the business to obtain goods now and pay later within agreed terms
questions.explanation: Trade credit can support working capital by delaying payment, but it must be managed within supplier terms.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain advantages and risks of short-term credit sources.

questions.prompt: Which factor should be checked before a small business takes a loan?
options: Ability to repay from expected cash flows
Whether records can be hidden from lenders
How to avoid reading loan terms
Whether stock can be valued at zero
questions.correctAnswer: Ability to repay from expected cash flows
questions.explanation: Responsible borrowing requires checking purpose, cost, repayment period, cash flow, and risks before accepting credit.
questions.learningOutcome: Assess factors to consider before borrowing for business.

questions.prompt: A business borrows 50,000 shillings at simple interest of 12 percent per year for two years. How much interest will it pay?
options: 12,000 shillings
6,000 shillings
62,000 shillings
100,000 shillings
questions.correctAnswer: 12,000 shillings
questions.explanation: Simple interest is principal multiplied by rate and time: 50,000 times 12 percent times two years equals 12,000 shillings.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate simple interest on business borrowing.

questions.prompt: Which practice best improves credit control in a business selling goods on credit?
options: Set credit limits, issue invoices promptly, and follow up overdue accounts
Allow every customer unlimited credit without records
Stop checking customer balances after delivery
Destroy invoices once goods leave the shop
questions.correctAnswer: Set credit limits, issue invoices promptly, and follow up overdue accounts
questions.explanation: Credit control reduces bad debts by setting clear terms, recording sales, monitoring balances, and collecting debts on time.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze methods of managing credit sales and debt collection.

questions.prompt: Which investment option usually represents ownership in a company?
options: Ordinary shares
Treasury bill
Fixed deposit account
Trade payable
questions.correctAnswer: Ordinary shares
questions.explanation: Ordinary shares give the holder an ownership interest in a company, with returns depending on dividends and share value.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish between common savings and investment options.

questions.prompt: Why should an investor be cautious about a scheme promising unusually high guaranteed returns in a few days?
options: High promised returns with little information can indicate fraud or excessive risk
Guaranteed fast returns are always approved by regulators
Risk disappears when an advert uses bright colours
A short deadline proves the investment is safe
questions.correctAnswer: High promised returns with little information can indicate fraud or excessive risk
questions.explanation: Unrealistic guaranteed returns, pressure to act quickly, and unclear registration details are warning signs that require verification.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate warning signs in investment offers.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes financial literacy for an entrepreneur?
options: The ability to make informed decisions about saving, borrowing, budgeting, investing, and risk
The ability to avoid keeping any business record
The habit of borrowing whenever money is available
The skill of setting prices without considering costs
questions.correctAnswer: The ability to make informed decisions about saving, borrowing, budgeting, investing, and risk
questions.explanation: Financial literacy helps entrepreneurs manage money, compare options, and protect the business from avoidable financial problems.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of financial literacy in enterprise success.

questions.prompt: Which activity is part of market segmentation?
options: Grouping customers by shared needs, location, income, or behaviour
Selling the same product at random to everyone without analysis
Recording depreciation on equipment
Reconciling the bank statement
questions.correctAnswer: Grouping customers by shared needs, location, income, or behaviour
questions.explanation: Market segmentation helps a business identify customer groups and design suitable products, prices, and promotion.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe how businesses segment markets to serve customers better.

questions.prompt: A youth enterprise sells affordable phone accessories near a college and promotes them through student groups. Which target market is it mainly serving?
options: Learners and young adults around the college
Retired farmers in another county
Industrial machinery importers
Hospitals buying theatre equipment
questions.correctAnswer: Learners and young adults around the college
questions.explanation: The product, location, price, and promotion point to students and nearby young customers as the target segment.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify target markets from business information.

questions.prompt: Which element of the marketing mix is concerned with how goods reach customers?
options: Place
Price
Product
Promotion
questions.correctAnswer: Place
questions.explanation: Place covers distribution channels, location, transport, and availability of goods or services to customers.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify elements of the marketing mix.

questions.prompt: A business improves packaging, quality, and after-sale service for its product. Which marketing mix element is being improved most directly?
options: Product
Place
Price
People's private income
questions.correctAnswer: Product
questions.explanation: Product decisions include features, quality, design, packaging, branding, and services connected to what is offered.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply marketing mix concepts to product decisions.

questions.prompt: Which pricing method adds a fixed percentage to cost to arrive at selling price?
options: Cost-plus pricing
Penetration pricing
Skimming pricing
Random pricing
questions.correctAnswer: Cost-plus pricing
questions.explanation: Cost-plus pricing sets price by adding a markup to the cost of producing or buying the item.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify pricing methods used in business.

questions.prompt: An item costs 800 shillings and is sold at a 25 percent markup on cost. What is the selling price?
options: 1,000 shillings
825 shillings
975 shillings
1,200 shillings
questions.correctAnswer: 1,000 shillings
questions.explanation: Markup is 25 percent of 800, which is 200; selling price is 800 plus 200.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate selling price using markup on cost.

questions.prompt: Which promotion method is most suitable for announcing a one-week discount to nearby customers quickly and at low cost?
options: A clear social media post and posters at the shop entrance
A hidden note in the stock room
A bank reconciliation statement
A private supplier invoice only
questions.correctAnswer: A clear social media post and posters at the shop entrance
questions.explanation: Local posters and digital posts can reach nearby customers quickly with a time-bound message.
questions.learningOutcome: Select suitable promotion methods for different business objectives.

questions.prompt: Which advertising message is most ethical?
options: A truthful message showing price, key features, and conditions of the offer
A message claiming a product cures every illness without evidence
A message hiding extra charges until after payment
A message using a competitor's brand name to confuse buyers
questions.correctAnswer: A truthful message showing price, key features, and conditions of the offer
questions.explanation: Ethical advertising is honest, clear, fair, and avoids misleading claims or unfair attacks on competitors.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply ethical principles to promotion and customer communication.

questions.prompt: Which customer feedback method would give a business both ratings and written suggestions after a service?
options: A short survey with rating scales and comment spaces
Guessing what customers think after they leave
Counting only the number of coins in the till
Ignoring complaints unless they are posted online
questions.correctAnswer: A short survey with rating scales and comment spaces
questions.explanation: Surveys can collect measurable ratings and open comments that help improve products and service.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose methods for collecting and using customer feedback.

questions.prompt: A business receives repeated complaints about late deliveries. Which response is best?
options: Investigate delivery records, identify causes, communicate honestly, and improve the process
Delete all complaints to protect the business image
Blame customers without checking evidence
Increase prices without addressing delays
questions.correctAnswer: Investigate delivery records, identify causes, communicate honestly, and improve the process
questions.explanation: Effective complaint handling uses evidence, respectful communication, and corrective action to protect customer trust.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze customer complaints and recommend service improvements.

questions.prompt: Which action best builds a strong brand for a small Kenyan enterprise?
options: Delivering consistent quality, clear identity, and reliable customer service
Changing the business name every week
Copying another firm's logo exactly
Using different weights for different customers secretly
questions.correctAnswer: Delivering consistent quality, clear identity, and reliable customer service
questions.explanation: A brand gains value when customers consistently associate it with quality, trust, identity, and good experience.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate actions that strengthen brand image and customer loyalty.

questions.prompt: A business has many first-time buyers but few repeat customers. Which marketing decision would best address this problem?
options: Improve after-sale service and follow up customer satisfaction
Stop recording customer complaints
Spend all funds on attracting only new buyers
Reduce product quality to cut costs
questions.correctAnswer: Improve after-sale service and follow up customer satisfaction
questions.explanation: Repeat buying depends on satisfaction, trust, value, and good service after the first sale.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze customer retention problems and choose suitable responses.

questions.prompt: Which retail channel combines physical selling with online ordering for customer convenience?
options: Omnichannel retailing
Pure barter trade
Silent partnership
Unrecorded cash sales
questions.correctAnswer: Omnichannel retailing
questions.explanation: Omnichannel retailing connects physical and digital channels so customers can discover, order, pay, or collect through different touchpoints.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain modern retail channels and their effect on customer convenience.

questions.prompt: Which role is mainly performed by a wholesaler in the chain of distribution?
options: Buying goods in bulk from producers and selling smaller quantities to retailers
Setting national tax policy for all sellers
Providing personal consumption only for households
Issuing bank statements to traders
questions.correctAnswer: Buying goods in bulk from producers and selling smaller quantities to retailers
questions.explanation: Wholesalers bridge producers and retailers by bulk buying, storage, breaking bulk, and sometimes offering credit or delivery.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe functions of wholesalers in distribution.

questions.prompt: A manufacturer sells directly to consumers through its website. Which intermediary is most likely reduced?
options: Retailer
Auditor
Banker
Bookkeeper
questions.correctAnswer: Retailer
questions.explanation: Direct online selling can shorten the distribution chain by reducing or removing the retail intermediary.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze how direct selling affects distribution channels.

questions.prompt: Which factor is most important when choosing transport for perishable vegetables from a farm to an urban market?
options: Speed, reliability, cost, and protection from spoilage
The colour of the driver's shirt only
Whether records can be avoided
The distance from the shop to the bank alone
questions.correctAnswer: Speed, reliability, cost, and protection from spoilage
questions.explanation: Perishable goods require transport decisions that balance quick delivery, safety, cost, and product condition.
questions.learningOutcome: Select suitable transport modes for different goods and business needs.

questions.prompt: Which warehousing function helps stabilize supply between harvest seasons and periods of high demand?
options: Storage of goods until they are needed
Changing bank interest rates
Preparing employee contracts
Replacing customer feedback
questions.correctAnswer: Storage of goods until they are needed
questions.explanation: Warehousing stores goods safely so they can be released when demand arises or supply is low.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain functions of warehousing in distribution.

questions.prompt: Which inventory control method assumes goods bought first are sold or issued first?
options: FIFO
LIFO
Straight-line depreciation
Double-entry balancing
questions.correctAnswer: FIFO
questions.explanation: FIFO means first in, first out; it is useful where older stock should be sold before newer stock.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify stock valuation and control methods.

questions.prompt: A shop sells food items with expiry dates. Which stock rotation practice is most suitable?
options: Place older stock where it will be sold before newer deliveries
Keep old stock hidden until it expires
Mix expired stock with fresh stock to clear shelves
Sell newer stock first and ignore dates
questions.correctAnswer: Place older stock where it will be sold before newer deliveries
questions.explanation: Stock rotation reduces waste and protects customers by ensuring older safe stock is sold before newer stock.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply stock control practices to perishable goods.

questions.prompt: Which trade document gives details of goods sent to a buyer but does not request payment?
options: Delivery note
Invoice
Credit note
Cheque counterfoil
questions.correctAnswer: Delivery note
questions.explanation: A delivery note accompanies goods and confirms items delivered; an invoice requests payment.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish trade documents used in buying and selling goods.

questions.prompt: Which document is used in international trade to show the country where goods were produced?
options: Certificate of origin
Petty cash voucher
Goods received note
Bank reconciliation statement
questions.correctAnswer: Certificate of origin
questions.explanation: A certificate of origin identifies the country in which exported goods were produced or manufactured.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify documents used in import and export trade.

questions.prompt: Which benefit of international trade is most direct for Kenyan consumers?
options: Access to goods and services not produced locally or not available in enough quantity
Removal of all local businesses from the economy
A guarantee that every imported item is cheaper
An end to the need for quality standards
questions.correctAnswer: Access to goods and services not produced locally or not available in enough quantity
questions.explanation: International trade widens choice by allowing countries to exchange goods and services they produce efficiently or lack locally.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain benefits and challenges of international trade.

questions.prompt: A business importing machinery should consider exchange rate changes because they can
options: alter the local currency cost of paying a foreign supplier
make source documents unnecessary
guarantee that imports are always cheaper
remove the need for transport documents
questions.correctAnswer: alter the local currency cost of paying a foreign supplier
questions.explanation: Exchange rate movements affect how much local currency is needed to settle foreign currency obligations.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze risks faced by businesses involved in import and export trade.

questions.prompt: Which e-commerce practice best protects customers and the business?
options: Use clear product information, secure payment channels, and reliable delivery tracking
Ask customers to share passwords in public comments
Hide return conditions until after delivery
Ignore complaints from online buyers
questions.correctAnswer: Use clear product information, secure payment channels, and reliable delivery tracking
questions.explanation: Trusted e-commerce depends on accurate information, secure payments, privacy, delivery reliability, and fair complaint handling.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate safe and ethical practices for online business transactions.

questions.prompt: Which digital record would best help an online seller confirm that an order has been paid for and dispatched?
options: An order management record linked to payment and delivery status
A handwritten poem about the product
A deleted chat message after payment
A personal shopping list unrelated to the sale
questions.correctAnswer: An order management record linked to payment and delivery status
questions.explanation: Digital order records connect customer details, payment status, items ordered, dispatch, and delivery evidence.
questions.learningOutcome: Use digital records to track online sales and customer orders.

questions.prompt: Why should a business protect customer data collected during online sales?
options: To respect privacy, reduce fraud risk, and comply with responsible business practice
To make it easier to sell passwords to strangers
To replace product quality with customer lists
To avoid giving receipts for online payments
questions.correctAnswer: To respect privacy, reduce fraud risk, and comply with responsible business practice
questions.explanation: Customer data should be collected for legitimate purposes, kept secure, and used responsibly to protect trust and safety.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of customer data protection in digital business.

questions.prompt: Which metric would best show whether a social media promotion increased online customer interest?
options: Number of product page visits, inquiries, or orders during the campaign
The owner's shoe size
The amount of dust on store shelves
The number of blank pages in a receipt book
questions.correctAnswer: Number of product page visits, inquiries, or orders during the campaign
questions.explanation: Digital marketing performance can be assessed through measurable responses such as reach, clicks, inquiries, conversions, and orders.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret simple digital marketing indicators for business decisions.

questions.prompt: Which action should a business take after detecting a fake online account using its brand name?
options: Warn customers, report the account, strengthen verification, and keep evidence
Pay the fake account to continue operating
Ignore the risk because online identity does not affect trust
Delete all official customer contacts
questions.correctAnswer: Warn customers, report the account, strengthen verification, and keep evidence
questions.explanation: Brand impersonation can harm customers and reputation, so the business should communicate clearly and preserve evidence for reporting.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a response plan for common digital business risks.

questions.prompt: Which statement best defines insurance in business?
options: A contract where an insurer compensates the insured for specified losses in exchange for premiums
A method of avoiding every possible business loss
A loan that never has to be repaid
A guarantee that goods will always sell
questions.correctAnswer: A contract where an insurer compensates the insured for specified losses in exchange for premiums
questions.explanation: Insurance pools risk so that specified losses can be compensated according to the policy terms.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe insurance and its role in business risk management.

questions.prompt: Which principle requires the insured to disclose all important facts that may affect an insurance contract?
options: Utmost good faith
Subrogation
Contribution
Average clause
questions.correctAnswer: Utmost good faith
questions.explanation: Utmost good faith means both parties, especially the proposer, must disclose material facts honestly before the contract is made.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain principles governing insurance contracts.

questions.prompt: Which principle prevents an insured person from making a profit from an insured loss?
options: Indemnity
Insurable interest
Proximate cause
Arbitration
questions.correctAnswer: Indemnity
questions.explanation: Indemnity restores the insured to the financial position before the loss, without allowing profit from the claim.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate insurance principles to claims settlement.

questions.prompt: A shop owner insures stock against fire because the owner would suffer financially if the stock burned. Which principle is shown?
options: Insurable interest
Contribution
Subrogation
Caveat emptor
questions.correctAnswer: Insurable interest
questions.explanation: Insurable interest exists when a person would suffer financial loss if the insured item is damaged or lost.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply insurance principles to business situations.

questions.prompt: Which insurance policy is most relevant for a business vehicle used to deliver goods?
options: Motor vehicle insurance
Marine insurance
Fidelity guarantee only
Life assurance for the owner only
questions.correctAnswer: Motor vehicle insurance
questions.explanation: Motor vehicle insurance covers specified risks connected with vehicles, including legal requirements and possible accident losses.
questions.learningOutcome: Select suitable insurance policies for business assets and risks.

questions.prompt: Why is risk assessment important before choosing an insurance policy?
options: It helps identify likely losses, value of assets, and suitable cover
It proves premiums should never be paid
It removes the need for reading policy terms
It changes every loss into profit
questions.correctAnswer: It helps identify likely losses, value of assets, and suitable cover
questions.explanation: Risk assessment guides the choice of cover by matching policy terms to the business's real exposure and capacity to pay premiums.
questions.learningOutcome: Assess business risks before selecting insurance cover.

questions.prompt: Which example shows risk reduction rather than risk transfer?
options: Installing fire extinguishers and training staff to use them
Buying fire insurance only
Claiming compensation after a fire
Taking a bank loan to replace burnt stock
questions.correctAnswer: Installing fire extinguishers and training staff to use them
questions.explanation: Risk reduction lowers the chance or impact of a loss, while insurance mainly transfers financial risk to an insurer.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare methods of managing business risks.

questions.prompt: A business underinsures stock worth 400,000 shillings for only 200,000 shillings. Which issue may reduce compensation after a partial loss?
options: Average clause
Unit of account
Brand loyalty
Cash discount
questions.correctAnswer: Average clause
questions.explanation: The average clause can reduce a claim where property is insured for less than its full value.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze how underinsurance affects claims settlement.

questions.prompt: Which organization is responsible for administering and collecting national taxes in Kenya?
options: Kenya Revenue Authority
Capital Markets Authority
Kenya National Bureau of Statistics
Public Service Commission
questions.correctAnswer: Kenya Revenue Authority
questions.explanation: The Kenya Revenue Authority administers and collects national government taxes according to tax laws.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify institutions involved in tax administration in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Which tax is charged on the value added to taxable goods and services at different stages of supply?
options: Value Added Tax
PAYE
Customs duty
Withholding tax on rent
questions.correctAnswer: Value Added Tax
questions.explanation: Value Added Tax is a consumption tax applied to taxable supplies as goods and services move through the supply chain.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain common taxes affecting businesses and consumers.

questions.prompt: PAYE is mainly associated with tax deducted from
options: employment income by an employer
stock held in a warehouse
cash discounts allowed to customers
goods returned to a supplier
questions.correctAnswer: employment income by an employer
questions.explanation: PAYE means Pay As You Earn and is deducted from employees' taxable employment income where applicable.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify taxes deducted from employment income.

questions.prompt: Which practice supports tax compliance by a small registered business?
options: Keeping accurate sales, purchase, payroll, and expense records
Issuing fake receipts to reduce income
Deleting electronic payment messages after each sale
Using two sets of books to mislead auditors
questions.correctAnswer: Keeping accurate sales, purchase, payroll, and expense records
questions.explanation: Reliable records help a business file returns, support claims, pay tax due, and respond to tax queries.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of accurate records in tax compliance.

questions.prompt: A business collects VAT from customers but uses the money for personal spending instead of remitting it as required. Which issue is shown?
options: Tax non-compliance and unethical handling of collected tax
Responsible tax planning
Inventory valuation
Favourable sales variance
questions.correctAnswer: Tax non-compliance and unethical handling of collected tax
questions.explanation: Taxes collected on behalf of government should be recorded and remitted according to the law; using them personally is unethical and risky.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze ethical issues in business tax practices.

questions.prompt: Which digital tool can help a business improve tax record accuracy?
options: An electronic invoicing or accounting system that records sales and purchases
A blank notebook kept away from transactions
A calculator used only for games
A social media rumour about tax rates
questions.correctAnswer: An electronic invoicing or accounting system that records sales and purchases
questions.explanation: Digital accounting and invoicing systems reduce errors, preserve records, and make filing or review easier.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply digital tools to business tax record keeping.

questions.prompt: Which consequence can result from deliberate tax evasion?
options: Penalties, interest, legal action, and damage to business reputation
Automatic increase in customer loyalty
A permanent exemption from keeping records
Guaranteed approval for bank loans
questions.correctAnswer: Penalties, interest, legal action, and damage to business reputation
questions.explanation: Tax evasion exposes a business to financial, legal, and reputation risks.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe consequences of failing to meet tax obligations.

questions.prompt: Which procurement practice is most transparent?
options: Comparing supplier quotations using price, quality, delivery time, and reliability
Choosing a supplier secretly because of a personal favour
Ignoring quality once the lowest price is seen
Buying without any written order or receipt
questions.correctAnswer: Comparing supplier quotations using price, quality, delivery time, and reliability
questions.explanation: Transparent procurement uses clear criteria, records, and fair comparison before selecting suppliers.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply fair procurement procedures in business purchasing.

questions.prompt: Which document is prepared by a department to ask the purchasing section to obtain goods?
options: Purchase requisition
Receipt
Statement of profit or loss
Credit note to customer
questions.correctAnswer: Purchase requisition
questions.explanation: A purchase requisition is an internal request for goods or services before a purchase order is issued.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify documents used in purchasing procedures.

questions.prompt: Which reason best supports using a goods received note?
options: It confirms the quantity and condition of goods received for checking against orders and invoices
It advertises goods to final consumers
It replaces the supplier's need to deliver goods
It records the owner's private drawings
questions.correctAnswer: It confirms the quantity and condition of goods received for checking against orders and invoices
questions.explanation: A goods received note supports internal control by recording what was actually received.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how purchasing documents support internal control.

questions.prompt: A business keeps too much slow-moving stock. Which cost is most likely to increase?
options: Storage, insurance, damage, and obsolescence costs
Customer satisfaction from fresh stock only
Speed of stock turnover
Cash available for other uses
questions.correctAnswer: Storage, insurance, damage, and obsolescence costs
questions.explanation: Excess inventory ties up cash and increases holding costs, spoilage, damage, theft, and outdated stock risk.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze the effects of overstocking and understocking.

questions.prompt: Which quality control action is most suitable for a bakery producing bread daily?
options: Checking ingredient measurements, baking time, hygiene, and sample product quality
Selling products before checking if they are baked
Changing recipes randomly without records
Ignoring customer complaints about stale bread
questions.correctAnswer: Checking ingredient measurements, baking time, hygiene, and sample product quality
questions.explanation: Quality control checks inputs, process conditions, hygiene, and outputs to maintain safe and consistent products.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply quality control methods to business production.

questions.prompt: Which measure would best improve productivity in a small tailoring business?
options: Training workers, arranging machines efficiently, and reducing material wastage
Increasing rework by ignoring measurements
Keeping machines unrepaired until they stop working
Hiding customer orders from employees
questions.correctAnswer: Training workers, arranging machines efficiently, and reducing material wastage
questions.explanation: Productivity improves when labour, materials, equipment, and time are used efficiently to produce quality output.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate methods of improving productivity in enterprise operations.

questions.prompt: Which action is an example of sustainable business operation?
options: Reducing waste, saving energy, and sourcing materials responsibly
Dumping packaging waste into a drainage channel
Using excess water because it is available today
Buying illegal materials to reduce costs
questions.correctAnswer: Reducing waste, saving energy, and sourcing materials responsibly
questions.explanation: Sustainable operations reduce harm to the environment and community while supporting long-term business performance.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply sustainable practices in business operations.

questions.prompt: Which labour document states job title, duties, pay, working hours, and other employment terms?
options: Contract of employment
Delivery note
Bank paying-in slip
Certificate of origin
questions.correctAnswer: Contract of employment
questions.explanation: A contract of employment records the agreed rights and duties of the employer and employee.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify documents used in employment relationships.

questions.prompt: Which practice best supports fair recruitment in a business?
options: Use job-related criteria and keep records of the selection process
Select relatives only without considering ability
Change requirements after seeing applicants' names
Hide the job advert from qualified candidates
questions.correctAnswer: Use job-related criteria and keep records of the selection process
questions.explanation: Fair recruitment applies relevant criteria consistently and keeps evidence of how decisions were made.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply fair procedures when recruiting employees.

questions.prompt: Which benefit is most likely from training employees on customer care and product knowledge?
options: Better service quality, fewer errors, and improved customer confidence
Automatic elimination of all business expenses
A guarantee that no competitor will enter the market
Permission to ignore customer complaints
questions.correctAnswer: Better service quality, fewer errors, and improved customer confidence
questions.explanation: Training can improve skill, confidence, productivity, and consistency in serving customers.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the value of employee training to business performance.

questions.prompt: Which workplace practice best protects employee safety in a workshop?
options: Provide protective equipment, safety instructions, and regular inspection of tools
Store sharp tools randomly on the floor
Ignore hazards until an accident occurs
Allow untrained employees to operate all machines
questions.correctAnswer: Provide protective equipment, safety instructions, and regular inspection of tools
questions.explanation: Workplace safety depends on prevention, training, protective equipment, maintenance, and reporting hazards early.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe workplace practices in business operations.

questions.prompt: A manager notices frequent lateness and declining output. Which response is most professional?
options: Discuss the issue with employees, review causes, agree targets, and monitor progress
Deduct random amounts from wages without records
Ignore the trend until customers complain
Dismiss everyone without checking policy or evidence
questions.correctAnswer: Discuss the issue with employees, review causes, agree targets, and monitor progress
questions.explanation: Performance management should be fair, evidence-based, respectful, and focused on improvement where possible.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze workplace performance issues and propose fair responses.

questions.prompt: Which leadership action best supports teamwork in a student enterprise project?
options: Assign roles clearly, listen to members, resolve conflicts fairly, and review progress
Keep all information with one person only
Blame members publicly without discussing solutions
Change goals daily without explanation
questions.correctAnswer: Assign roles clearly, listen to members, resolve conflicts fairly, and review progress
questions.explanation: Effective leadership builds teamwork through clarity, participation, accountability, communication, and fair conflict resolution.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate leadership practices that improve enterprise teamwork.

questions.prompt: A learner team wants to start a low-cost refill stationery service in school. Which first step best supports a realistic business plan?
options: Research demand, costs, suppliers, rules, risks, and available resources
Buy large stock before asking whether learners need refills
Set a selling price without checking costs
Start selling without recording any transaction
questions.correctAnswer: Research demand, costs, suppliers, rules, risks, and available resources
questions.explanation: A realistic plan starts with evidence about customers, costs, operations, resources, compliance, and risks.
questions.learningOutcome: Create an evidence-based approach to planning a small enterprise.

questions.prompt: Which set of sections would make a simple but complete business plan for a Grade 11 enterprise project?
options: Business idea, market analysis, operations plan, financial plan, risk plan, and implementation schedule
Business name only and a list of friends
A sales slogan without costs or customers
A bank deposit slip and no explanation of the business
questions.correctAnswer: Business idea, market analysis, operations plan, financial plan, risk plan, and implementation schedule
questions.explanation: A useful business plan connects the opportunity, customers, operations, finances, risks, and actions needed to implement the idea.
questions.learningOutcome: Organize key sections of a practical business plan.
